name: TubeHaus
subtitle: A private YouTube client
description: TubeHaus for iPad and iPhone: no Google account, recommendations kept on the device. Open source (AGPL-3.0).

apps.name: TubeHaus
apps.subtitle: A private YouTube client
apps.localizedDescription:
TubeHaus is a YouTube client that needs no Google account and keeps what you watch on your device.

- Apple's player, background play and picture-in-picture
- Subscriptions without an account
- Recommendations worked out on the device; tell it to forget a video or a channel
- Import subscriptions from Google Takeout (CSV), NewPipe, FreeTube or Invidious
- Calm mode and Focus: hide Shorts, comments, related videos or thumbnails
- Optional: connect to your own self-hosted TubeHaus server

Beta. Not affiliated with YouTube or Google.

versions.localizedDescription: 1.6.0: the same version as the TubeHaus server 1.6, "Back to music" in the music player, and small fixes.
1.5.1: opening a video no longer closes the app (#67), importing from FreeTube and Google Takeout (several files at once), and waiting and retrying when YouTube says too many requests.

1.5.0: the TubeHaus 1.5 design, a new Music home, video at a glance (key moments and chapters from the captions), nearby devices on your Wi-Fi, kids mode, and saving new videos of a channel automatically.

1.0.6: ...more under a video no longer closes the app, the full-screen button turns the iPhone picture sideways, Check for updates works, and the AirPlay button matches the others and lights up while playing on a TV.

1.0.5: a queue (Play next, Add to queue), full screen when the iPhone is turned sideways, switches for gestures, the AirPlay button, the Music tab and the logo, and fixes for the AirPlay button and the seek bar.
1.0.4: caption size, background and position in Settings → Player.
1.0.3: works with VoiceOver: buttons, filter chips and switches say what they are, and the seek bar and volume can be read and moved.
1.0.2: the transcript in any caption language, saved as text, SRT or WebVTT; search by fewest views, oldest first and a view count range.
1.0.1: what plays shows in Control Center and on the lock screen, with its buttons; a save that the system refuses for a moment is tried again and never closes the app.

Shared with the 1.0.0 release: the look of the web app 1.0, with the Pretendard font, softer colours, pill tabs, rounder cards, and Settings on one page of cards with a menu that jumps to each category.

Shared with the 0.5.19 release: a Music tab (songs, albums, artists, lyrics, radio and a queue), searchable transcripts, A-B repeat, speed remembered for each channel, watch time with break reminders, and Settings with search and categories.

Shared with the 0.5.18 release: AirPlay from the player, taste profiles (separate recommendations for separate moods, export and import), and eight more languages: Chinese, Portuguese, French, Russian, Hindi, Indonesian, Turkish and Bengali.

Shared with the 0.5.17 release: Spanish, Japanese and German, view counts read right in every language, no clock and battery over fullscreen videos, a button to update the YouTube engine, and ...more no longer closing the app.

Shared with the 0.5.16 release: YouTube's topic pages (Music, Live, News, Sports and more), SponsorBlock with Jump to the highlight, dislike counts, DeArrow titles and thumbnails, the "Most replayed" wave, and channel pictures on every card.

Shared with the 0.5.15 release: YouTube-like channel pages, chapters, seek bar previews, search filters, comment sorts, loop, sleep timer and stats for nerds, what's new in the app, and better subscription groups.
Shared with the 0.5.13 release: when the player refuses a video's streams (for example after switching Wi-Fi, mobile data or a VPN), the app fetches fresh ones once and carries on where it stopped.
Shared with the 0.5.11 release: the original audio track is chosen first, plus caption and player sheet updates.
Same version as the Android fix release; no changes on iPad and iPhone.
The channel picture on the watch page shows again when YouTube leaves it out.
iPad: details and comments under the video like YouTube on a computer, up next beside it. Videos play through the connected TubeHaus server when one is connected.
